image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile resting in shallow water or on a muddy bank. The crocodile is facing the camera with its mouth slightly open, revealing teeth. Its body is covered in rough, armored scales (scutes). The background consists of earthy tones, likely a rock wall or mud bank, and some rocks in the foreground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is clearly visible, showing the characteristic broad base tapering to a V-shaped snout, distinct from the U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is slightly agape, revealing multiple conical teeth. The fourth lower tooth appears to fit into the upper jaw notch, consistent with crocodile anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eyes are clearly positioned on top of the head. While pupil shape is hard to resolve at this resolution, the dorsal positioning is correct. Nictitating membrane is not clearly visible but eyes appear structurally sound.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating. Elongation is implied by the species, though only the anterior half is fully visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture is highly detailed, showing distinct, rough scutes arranged in rows along the back and neck.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration matches the description (grey/brown/greenish mix) and the texture is visibly rough and bony.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodile is viewed from above; the belly (ventral surface) is completely occluded by the body and the ground/water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One forelimb is visible tucked under the body, appearing short and stout. A hind limb is partially visible in the background. Digit counting is difficult due to angle/occlusion, but general morphology is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail extends out of the frame or is obscured by the body angle and background elements; its full length and compression cannot be verified.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the image, background rock/ground interface
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight blurring and lack of definition where the crocodile's right flank meets the background rock. It looks slightly 'painted on' rather than physically interacting with the environment, suggesting minor segmentation or generation softness.

The hind foot in the upper center background appears somewhat malformed and fused with the ground texture. The digits are not clearly defined, looking more like a lump of texture than a distinct webbed foot.
